free_tier.stated: 2 GiB free per ORGANIZATION (not per project, not per feed), then tiered per-GiB: 2–10 GiB $2/GiB, 10–100 GiB $1/GiB, 100–1,000 GiB $0.50/GiB, 1,000+ GiB $0.25/GiB.

retention.stated: | 2 GiB total across all feeds in the org; exceeding it makes the org read-only for publishing until you delete data or add billing; Public feeds only exist inside 'public projects', and Microsoft is retiring public projects — 'Starting in 2027, existing public projects will automatically convert to private, and public feeds will no longer be publicly accessible.'

egress.terms: No separate egress SKU for Azure Artifacts; The metered dimension is storage only, which is unusual and mildly favourable — but 2 GiB is the binding constraint long before bandwidth.

interface_detail: rest (Azure DevOps Artifacts API), NuGet/npm/Maven/Python/Cargo/Universal Package clients, `az artifacts universal`
tooling: `nuget push`, `npm publish`, `twine upload`, `mvn deploy`, `az artifacts universal publish`; documented upstream-source proxying for public registries.
chaining: Per-org 2 GiB × unlimited free Azure DevOps organizations (each needs a Microsoft account and an org). Note the free tier is per org and pools across all projects in it — you cannot multiply by adding projects or feeds.
limits_note: 2 GiB total across all feeds in the org; exceeding it makes the org read-only for publishing until you delete data or add billing; Public feeds only exist inside 'public projects', and Microsoft is retiring public projects — 'Starting in 2027, existing public projects will automatically convert to private, and public feeds will no longer be publicly accessible.'
reliability_note: Rock solid technically, but the public-feed capability has a published 2027 end date, which kills the anonymous-fetch use case.
